passages.title: Rising Star: An Interview with Leo Vance
passages.text: At just sixteen years old, Leo Vance has already made a name for himself in the world of competitive swimming. We caught up with him at his local training pool to talk about his recent success at the National Youth Championships. 'It was a dream come true,' Leo says, still sounding surprised by his gold medal. 'I’ve been training since I was six, but I never expected to win against such experienced swimmers.' Leo’s daily routine is far from typical for a teenager. He wakes up at 4:30 a.m. every single day to swim for two hours before school starts. After classes, he heads back to the pool for another session. 'It’s tough, especially in the winter when it’s cold and dark,' he admits. 'But when I’m in the water, I forget everything else. It’s my happy place.' His coach, Sarah Jenkins, believes Leo’s success is down to his mental strength. 'Many young athletes have talent, but Leo has the discipline to keep going even when he’s tired. He doesn’t just want to win; he wants to improve his personal best every time he competes.' Despite the pressure, Leo remains grounded. He still finds time to see his friends on weekends and enjoys playing video games, though he admits he has to be careful with his diet. Looking ahead, Leo is already focused on his next goal: qualifying for the international junior team. 'It’s a big step,' he says, 'but I’m ready to work for it.' With his determination and support system, it seems likely that we will be seeing much more of Leo in the future.

questions.question: How did Leo feel about winning the gold medal?
questions.explanation: Leo mentions he was surprised by the win despite his years of training.
options: a) He felt it was expected after years of training.
b) He was disappointed that the competition was easy.
c) He was surprised because he was competing against more experienced swimmers.
d) He felt relieved that his training was finally over.

questions.question: What does Leo say about his training routine?
questions.explanation: Leo describes his routine as tough, particularly in winter, but finds it enjoyable.
options: a) He finds it easy to wake up early every day.
b) He finds it difficult during the winter months.
c) He prefers training in the afternoon rather than the morning.
d) He thinks his routine is typical for a teenager.

questions.question: According to his coach, what makes Leo a special athlete?
questions.explanation: The coach highlights his mental strength and discipline as the key factors.
options: a) He has the discipline to keep training even when exhausted.
b) He is naturally more talented than all other swimmers.
c) He is only interested in winning medals.
d) He never feels tired during his training sessions.

questions.question: What does the text say about Leo's life outside of swimming?
questions.explanation: Leo manages to maintain a social life and hobbies despite his training schedule.
options: a) He has no time for friends because of his training.
b) He is not allowed to play video games.
c) He has to follow a very strict diet with no exceptions.
d) He makes time for friends and hobbies on the weekend.

questions.question: What is Leo's main goal for the near future?
questions.explanation: Leo explicitly mentions his goal of qualifying for the international junior team.
options: a) To win another gold medal at the national level.
b) To change his coach and training methods.
c) To get a place on the international junior team.
d) To stop swimming and focus on his schoolwork.
